lines.en: What we call success is often only the visible tip of ten years of invisible work.
It is not the achievement that changes a person, but the person they had to become to reach it.
Were success purely a matter of talent, the most talented would never fail, and they fail daily.
However high you climb, the view is rented, never owned; yesterday's champion is tomorrow's memory.
Not until he reached the top did he understand why everyone warned him about the emptiness there.
It is said that success has many fathers, while failure is an orphan.
What she built, in the end, was not the company she had dreamed of, but something the dream had never imagined.
The prize, when it finally came, meant less to him than the letter from the student it had inspired.
Little does the audience see of the doubt that visits every performer in the minute before the lights.
Rarely is the summit the point; the climb is.
What the biography celebrates in one chapter cost the people around him ten quiet years.
It is worth asking, at every stage, whether the ladder is leaning against the right wall.
Were he given the choice again, he said, he would trade one of the awards for the dinners he missed.
Not until the applause stops do most performers meet the person they actually are.
However many the trophies, they gather dust; the work that earned them keeps its shine.
